newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGER BLASTS ABSENT SALE PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGER BLASTS ABSENT SALE PLAYERS.

text.p: British Lions manager Fran Cotton launched a broadside at the Sale players who opted out of the North's match against the New Zealand Barbarians on Sunday.

The eight-strong contingent from the English division one side pulled out on Friday because they were "concerned over potential injuries in unequal contests" and were replaced largely by players from division two sides Wakefield and Rotherham.
The North went down 86-0, conceding 14 tries, to a virtually full-strength All Blacks team who took the opportunity to flex their considerable muscle for Saturday's clash with England at Twickenham.

"I was embarrassed by the actions of the Sale players, I'm totally ashamed of them," said Cotton, the former England captain and North chairman who will manage the Lions in South Africa next summer. "They let themselves, their club and the North of England down. "
The North had just one training session before taking on the might of Jonah Lomu and company but Cotton was full of praise for the patched-up side.
"It was an impossible task but I was very proud of them. They played with a lot of spirit and did as well as anybody could have expected."

The Barbarians set the platform for their romp with a storming forward display which brought first half tries for flankers Andrew Blowers (two) and Dylan Mika, prop Olo Brown, number eight Taine Randell and full back Chris Cullen.
The one-way traffic continued after the break withViri registering his hat-trick and other tries coming from Spencer (two), Robin Brooke and Mark Robinson.
